classification.difficultyReason: Read centres and radius information from diagrams, using Pythagoras where the radius is not supplied.

content.prompt: Determine the equation of each circle, using Pythagoras if necessary to find the radius.

spec.description: Circle with centre aligned with axis ticks 2 and 3; dashed upper-right radius identified by a curved pointer labelled 1. Ordinary source marks use house black.
spec.answerVisibility: All givens remain visible in the question; no equation answer is printed.

spec.description: Circle with centre aligned with ticks -2 and -1 and dashed lower-left radius labelled 2. The circle is tangent to the y-axis. Ordinary source marks use house black.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied diagram givens are visible.

spec.description: Circle with centre labelled (-1,1) and upper y-intercept labelled 4. No radius construction is supplied. Ordinary source marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: Centre (-1,1), point (0,4) on the circle, radius squared 10.
spec.answerVisibility: The centre and intercept are permanent givens; the radius and equation are answers.

answer.worked:
The circle passes through $(0,4)$. Using Pythagoras,
$$\begin{aligned}r^2&=(0-(-1))^2+(4-1)^2\\&=1^2+3^2\\&=10\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$(x+1)^2+(y-1)^2=10.$$

spec.description: Circle with centre labelled (2,-1), passing through the origin. No radius construction is supplied. Ordinary source marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: Centre (2,-1), radius squared 5; the origin lies on the circle.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied centre and circle remain visible; the equation is hidden in the question edition.

answer.worked:
The circle passes through the origin. Using Pythagoras,
$$\begin{aligned}r^2&=2^2+(-1)^2\\&=4+1\\&=5\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$(x-2)^2+(y+1)^2=5.$$
